key_insight: The paper proposes CMA-AL, a six-level hierarchy that defines how computational materials science systems can progress from scripted workflows to self-extending autonomous discovery.
engineering_relevance: CMA-AL gives researchers and platform builders a shared framework to benchmark autonomy, compare agentic materials systems, and design safer paths toward self-driving materials discovery.
method: Defines six autonomy levels: scripted executor, LLM-assisted operator, adaptive explorer, experiment-ready modeler, agentic digital twin, and self-extending intelligence.
Maps emerging agentic systems onto the hierarchy to assess their current maturity.
Identifies scientific and technological challenges needed to reach higher autonomy.
evidence_signal: The abstract frames the work as a Perspective and framework proposal, with evaluation based on conceptual taxonomy and mapping rather than new experimental data.
watch_item: Higher autonomy may be difficult to validate in practice because scientific decision-making, reliability, and safety become harder to control as systems move beyond human-directed workflows.
paper_title: From Automated Simulation to Autonomous Discovery: A Hierarchical Framework for Agentic Computational Materials Science
